theme: MAJ: major links (narrowed test, institutional acts only; adoption by vote is minor)
checked: All 91 links that carry outcome: every quote re-found verbatim at its lines (91/91 links, 0 misses), each outcome read against the vendored file around its cited lines, and P2-ML's Final.json evidence lines for eras 1-5 compared with each link's listed sources (8 off the link: 4 secondary-only links whose vendored secondaries do show the act, and 4 real gaps). All 91 outcomes scored with score_turn (all pass; 1 sentence of 26 words), word counts (all <=30) and a British-spelling scan (none). For consistency: 101 judged-type links without outcome whose note or quotes contain act words (condemn, council, synod, decree, bull, law, banish, depose and so on), read against P2-ML's reasons and the era 6-9 outcome_considered and minor_reason records; plus a script listing every judged-type link in eras 1-9 that no pass judged for outcome (4 found, all era 6, 'on main (earlier)'). The 7 outcome_no_primary links in mech.json were each checked.

findings.finding: The Council of Constance's sentence on Hus (condemned for heresy, degraded, handed to the secular court) is shown by this link's own quote, yet the link carries no outcome. It was never judged: it was on main before era 6, and the era-6 pass judged only links it drafted (its README table marks it 'on main (earlier)'), while P2-ML covered only eras 1-5. Comparable council condemnations are major elsewhere: the Council of Vienne on the beguines and the Free Spirit (same papal movement, era 6), Lateran IV on Joachim's book (era 5), Constantinople II on Theodore of Mopsuestia (era 3), Aquileia on Palladius (era 2).

findings.finding: The outcome is the 410 synod's own canon adopting the western order of worship taught by Isaac and Marutha. That is a church body adopting another side's worship order by its own vote, which the ruling of 2026-11-08 ('adoption by vote is minor') makes minor. P2-ML judged it before that ruling and itself called it 'Practice taken up by synod' (Opus_Review_Round1.json). The same class was dropped elsewhere: the Scottish General Assembly 1562 and Paris 1559 (era 7), the Moscow council of 1656 on the corrected service book and Zamość 1720 (era 8), Trent's Vulgate decree (removed from P2-ML's own set).

checked_and_fine: outcome_no_primary (mech.json), 7 links: Dvin 554 (Ormanian 2550-2556), Nerses Bakur (Ormanian 2902-2907), Humiliati approval 1200 (Giussano 12177-12179), Basil the Bogomil burned (Rački 1735-1752), Edinoverie 1800 (Conybeare 5533-5536), Kyiv to Moscow 1686 (Mouravieff 11424-11427) and Catherine II 1795 (Pelesz 41250-41254). In each, a vendored secondary on the link states the act; all are graded DMR. Nerses Bakur is still part of MAJ-06.
Charlemagne 802 and Carloman 742 imposing the Rule of Benedict: a ruler's order binding other houses, not a body adopting a text by its own vote. Major stands.

Borromean Milan 1565 (provincial council taxes benefices to found a seminary, at Trent's order): a new funding rule made by an authority in obedience to a higher council. It differs from Zamość 1720, where the synod received Trent and adopted Latin feasts. Major stands, though it is the nearest case to the adoption class after MAJ-04/05.

Florence 1439 (major, era 6) against Lyon 1274 (minor, era 5): Lyon's link shows only a Greek profession of faith, while Florence's shows a council decree with a stated rule (leavened or unleavened bread). Consistent.

Kyiv synod 1628 on Smotrytsky's Apology (era 7, minor): the source has an envoy reporting the synod's opinion before any sentence. Era 1's Montanist meetings show the act itself ('rejected them as heretical' and expulsion). Consistent.

Readmissions by an authority: Nicaea II receiving iconoclast bishops (era 4), Dioscorus receiving separated parties (era 3), the Basel legates receiving the Prague masters (era 6) and the Synod receiving the Uniates in 1839 (era 9) are all major. Oura 1865 (era 9, minor) shows no act by any authority. Consistent.

'One bishop's excommunication does not count' (Callistus and Sabellius, Demetrius and Origen, the 1054 legates, eras 1-5; Ethiopia, era 7) against Rome expelling Marcion and Valentinus (era 1, major): P2-ML ruled 'the church' expelling them differs from one bishop's act, and round 1 settled it inside era 1. Not cross-era, so not re-opened.
